answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A karst delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A vault check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A yarrow penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 6808 identities need 6808 bonds of 33 tokens, 37197 dollars of hardware and 18 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
